title: The module form of the classical equivalence
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a discrete commutative ring, $\Lambda_{X,\Et}$ its constant
sheaf on $X_{\Et}$, and identify $\Lambda_X=\nu_X^*\Lambda_{X,\Et}$. Then
$\nu_X^*$ and $\nu_{X,*}$ restrict to an adjoint pair between
$\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ and $\Mod(X_{\Proet},\Lambda_X)$; the functor
$\nu_X^*\colon\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)\to\Mod(X_{\Proet},\Lambda_X)$ is exact and
fully faithful, and it is an equivalence onto the full subcategory of
classical $\Lambda_X$-module sheaves, with quasi-inverse $\nu_{X,*}$.

proof.text: Specialize the canonical comparison adjunction comparisonAdjunction to ModuleCat over the arbitrary commutative ring. The already proved source-library instance preservesFiniteLimits_comparisonUpperStar gives finite-limit preservation directly; the left adjoint preserves all colimits, hence finite colimits. These constructions have no finite-ring hypothesis.

proof.text: The forgetful functor ModuleCat to sets preserves filtered colimits (Mathlib ModuleCat.FilteredColimits.forget_preservesFilteredColimits). The comma categories for toProEt.op are filtered by the representable flatness of the site inclusion. Therefore forgetting preserves these pointwise left Kan extensions. It preserves sheafification as well. Apply the canonical sheafPullbackForgetIso to identify module inverse image followed by forgetting with forgetting followed by set inverse image.

proof.text: At the restriction of G, the unit compatibility of sheafPullbackForgetIso says V(eta) followed by Rset(e.hom) equals etaSet. Compose with Rset(e.inv) and cancel the inverse comparison. Apply the set adjunction Hom equivalence to e.inv followed by the forgotten module counit. The preceding equation turns its adjunct into V(eta) followed by V(R(epsilon)), which is the identity by the module right triangle identity. The adjunct of the set counit is the identity by the set right triangle identity. Injectivity of the Hom equivalence proves equality with the set counit.

proof.text: Apply the counit characterization of det-pe-classical-sheaves-image to the underlying set sheaf of G. Step 3 identifies the set counit with the forgotten module counit composed with an isomorphism. Forgetting module sheaves reflects isomorphisms, sectionwise because a bijective linear map has a linear inverse. Thus G has classical underlying set sheaf exactly when its module counit is invertible. This uses the existing classicality predicate without introducing another one.

proof.text: The existing generic Grothendieck abelian comparison-unit theorem specializes to ModuleCat and gives the source-library full and faithful instances. Functor.FullyFaithful.ofFullyFaithful.map_bijective gives the required Hom-set bijections. Mathlib Adjunction.isIso_counit_app_iff_mem_essImage identifies the invertible module counit with existence of an etale module sheaf and an isomorphism of its inverse image with G. Compose this equivalence with step 4. These are precisely the last two clauses, and all statements and universes are unchanged.

split_report.summary: Five steps implement the four blueprint paragraphs: explicit transport of module structures and the adjunction, arbitrary-coefficient exactness, full faithfulness including addition and zero, the elementary module/set filtered-colimit comparison, and the linear unit/counit equivalence. Reused existing nodes only. The finite-coefficient theorem cannot be applied to arbitrary discrete rings, so exactness uses the generic abelian site theorem and the existing module-forgetful kernel/cokernel theorem.
split_report.blueprint: Steps 1, 2 and 3 realize paragraphs 1, 2 and 3 of the module proof; steps 4 and 5 supply paragraph 4. This is the module clause in the last sentence of the recognizing-classical-part unit proof. No unit or chapter route is replaced.

tool_uses.why: Generic exactness of abelian inverse image is needed in paragraph 2 for arbitrary discrete coefficients; the unit's finite-ring comparison theorem does not cover those coefficients.

Generic preservation of kernels and cokernels by the module-to-abelian forgetful functor converts abelian exactness into module exactness; the classical-equivalence unit has no such general module theorem.
